# dsh-kanban
One task board for the whole home directory, shared by Dhira and by every agent session: the panel i

s
the human's view, the `kanban_*` tools are the agents', and `bin/kanban.mjs` is the scripted one —

all
over one SQLite store, through one policy engine, so **the gate that refuses an agent is the ga

te that
refuses the human**.
| surface | who uses it | what it does |
| **Kanban panel** (`sidebar.panellist` → `main`) | the human | every state as a lane (`dropped` las
t), drag-and-drop with a keyboard path, a search box, a `New card` button that opens a minimal creat

e dialog, the card drawer with both checklists, the flow metrics and a collapsible history |
| **`ka
nban_*` tools** (9) and the `kanban` skill | agents | list, read, create, update/fill, move, drop, s

print, board, metrics — including the card's write scope |
| **`bin/kanban.mjs`** | the human, scrip
ts, checks | the same verbs from a shell, with distinct exit codes |
## Why

Task state used to live in a hand-authored Markdown table and in whatever each session remembered,
a
nd no surface could be trusted to agree with another: nothing enforced a gate, and nothing recorded

that a move had happened. The figures were the giveaway. An import stamped
`started_at = finished_at
= now` on eleven migrated cards, and the generated view advertised
> Throughput 11 in 7 days · Cycle time median 0d · SLE … (history, from 11 finished)

while the event log held two moves. A board that asserts history it does not have is worse than no
b
oard, because the number is read as evidence.
`dsh-kanban` replaces that with one SQLite store below all three surfaces and one policy engine abov

e
it, at `$DSH_HOME/.kanban/board.db`. The gates — Definition of Ready, Definition of Done, WIP limi

ts,
priority and class of service — live in the store; every mutation appends an event. The store is

the
only copy: the Markdown mirror and the per-card folder tree it once rendered are gone. The four

flow
metrics are recomputed from what happened rather than read off a column.
## Agent Skills
The host half registers the **`kanban`** skill at runtime, so an agent session can work a card witho

ut
reading this source: list and read the board, create a card, refine it until the Definition of Re

ady
is ticked, move it through the gates, comment, block and unblock — and be refused with the names

of
the items that are missing. The skill carries the DoR/DoD item names and the rule that a write s

cope
is data the agent must pass.
## Quick Start
The plugin lives inside the profile it serves, so "install" means *register it and restart the app*.
Either route ends the same way: a `link:` dependency, a bundle row, and a restart.
### Option A — the script
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Option B — by hand
1. **Clone it to a stable path** — the path becomes the install path.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

2. **`pnpm install`** — this plugin's own toolchain, not the profile's. Its `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
al

lows esbuild's build script, which pnpm 11 blocks by default. The `prepare` script runs
`node build.

mjs`, which writes `lib/**` (the host half, the store and the client half) and
`bin/kanban.mjs` — wh

at `main` and the bundle point at.
3. **Register the dependency *and* the bundle name** in the profi

le's `package.json`
(`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`):
[该节后续省略]
## How it Works

Three surfaces read and write **one** store through **one** policy engine: a rule enforced in the
pa
nel is enforced in the tools and the CLI, because there is only one implementation of it. The board
is `$DSH_HOME/.kanban/board.db` (SQLite), and its history is the append-only `events` table — one ro

w
per mutation. It is the only copy: no Markdown view and no folder tree, so never hand-edit it.
A profile plugin **cannot import anything but Node builtins** (`@deepseek-ai/*` does not resolve fro

m
a profile directory). That is why the DSH contracts are vendored in `src/types/dsh.ts`, the store

is
our own SQLite, and the browser half talks to the host over this plugin's own HTTP route rather t

han a
typed Remote. `DESIGN.md` is the full design record and `PRODUCT.md` the product brief.
`/api/kanban` serves `health`, `board` (with `?since=<rev>` → `304`), `task/:id`, and `POST mutate`

with an op. The route is registered as a prefix on the app's own web server, so it wins
the longest-

prefix match over the app's `/api` bridge and therefore **does not carry that bridge's
browser-sessi

on fence**: a request from this machine is believed, including an
`x-kanban-actor: human`. The serve
r binds loopback only.

That is a deliberate, recorded trade for a single-user local tool. The boundary that matters — an
ag

ent may not set a priority — is enforced at the *tool* boundary, where an agent's identity is its
se

ssion and not a header it can choose. A per-launch token is the obvious hardening and is deferred
un
til the index-injection question for a `file://`-loaded window is answered.
### What it looks like
The board, six lanes and every state reachable, in the app's own two themes. Nothing is styled again

st
the app: every colour is one of its theme tokens with a literal fallback.
| light | dark |
A card's drawer: one primary move, the rest behind a disclosure, the Definition of Ready as checkabl

e
rows, and the history collapsed until asked for.
| light | dark |
### Requirements

**Build-time:** Node 22 or newer (the host half is emitted for `node22`, and the suite uses
`--test-

isolation=none`), plus pnpm and the devDependencies — esbuild, TypeScript, React, jsdom. A
clone nee
ds nothing but `pnpm install`.

**Run-time:** the DSH desktop app. The built `lib/**` needs no install step of its own and no
devDep

endencies; the store uses `node:sqlite`, which ships with the app's Node. `bin/kanban.mjs` is a
bund

led ESM executable that imports nothing but Node builtins, so it runs from a clean checkout with
no

ble that imports nothing but Node builtins, so it runs from a clean checkout with
no `node_modules`.
